 Crm-M-48018-2025(O&M)
 Date of Decision: 04.11.2025
Arjun ..Petitioner
 Versus
State of Punjab & anr. ..Respondent

Coram: Hon'Ble Ms. Justice Shalini Singh Nagpal Present: Mr. Sunpreet Singh,
Advocate and Mr. Gurmehar Sekhon, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Hardeep Singh Wadhwa, Dag Punjab.
Shalini Singh Nagpal, Judge
1.  Petitioner seeks regular bail in FIR No.54 dated 25.07.2024 under Sections 137(2), 96 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, Police Station Daba, District Police Commissionerate Ludhiana.
Section 64 of BNS and 6 of POCSO Act added in the FIR during investigation.
This is his first petition for regular bail.
2. As per allegations, complainant, mother of the prosecutrix informed the police that she had two daughters and her elder daughter was 17 years old.
On 01.07.2024 at 04.00 PM, when she returned home, she found her daughter missing.
Despite efforts, she could not be traced.

She learnt that 'S'
had gone away with Akash, Ballu and Naresh Kumar alias Sonu.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that there was much delay in registration of the FIR,
wherein petitioner was not named.

It is submitted that the FIR was registered against Akash, Balu and Naresh Kumar alias Sonu Behnwal and it was on supplementary statement made by 1 of 3 CRM-M-48018-2025(O&M) -2- the complainant on 01.06.2025 that petitioner had been involved invoking Sections 6 of POCSO Act and 376 IPC.
It is further argued that prosecutrix had not pointed accusing finger at petitioner in her statement recorded during investigation.
Petitioner, who was in judicial custody for the last 6 months and 10 days deserved to be enlarged on regular bail.

4. Status report by way of affidavit of Satwinder Singh Virk, PPS Assistant Commissioner of Police,
Industrial Area-B, Ludhiana, has been filed by State of Haryana besides custody certificate of the petitioner.

Learned State counsel has opposed the prayer for bail arguing that there were serious allegations against the petitioner relating to offence under Section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Complainant alleged that her minor daughter was taken by the Arjun vs State Of Punjab on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8106012/
1 petitioner to Gaziabad where he made forcible relations with her.

Report of DNA examination was still awaited and considering the active role attributed to the petitioner, he did not deserve the concession of bail as his release may seriously prejudice prosecution case.
5. In her statement under Section 183 BNSS, prosecutrix stated that she had relations with Akash for few months and he had run away from his house.
On asking of her maternal aunt, Akash came back home.
Out of fear, she left her house and stayed for a few days in Amritsar Gurudwara where she did some jobs.
She slept in the Gurudwara.
She stated that no one was responsible and Arjun had only supported her.
He met her in the month of September and he was not at fault.
6. Petitioner is in judicial custody in the case for the last 6 months and 10 days.
His antecedents are clean.
There is no reason to believe that 2 of 3 CRM-M-48018-2025(O&M) -3- he would evade the process of law or tamper with evidence.
Considering the entire factual scenario of the case and the period of custody, petitioner has undergone, but without expressing any opinion on merits, the petition is allowed.
Petitioner is ordered to be released on regular bail, subject to his furnishing adequate bail and surety bonds to the satisfaction of trial Court/Duty Magistrate.
7. All the pending miscellaneous applications, if any, stand disposed of.
